scenes.say: Ever wonder why Spark crunches big data so quickly? What's its real secret sauce?

scenes.label: Lazy
scenes.sub: Spark waits to run code until you call an action.
scenes.say: The answer is lazy evaluation. Spark doesn't run your code right away. It waits until you ask for results.
Here's what happens. The driver plans the job. Executors run tasks on chunks of data called partitions. This means lots of work happens at once.
Some operations, like map or filter, only need one partition. Others, like group by or join, shuffle data between partitions. Shuffles can slow things down.

scenes.question: When does Spark run your code?
scenes.right: Only when you call an action, like count or collect.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap. Many think Spark runs code after each step. Nope. It only runs when you call an action, like count or collect.
